mechanism_verification.step1_causal_chain: research/FORMULATION.md scopes Context Inertia as a PHYSICAL cost that grows with context length, and StudyE10c section 6 / StudyE10d located its mechanism in this engine: a cold history prefill is ONE non-preemptive unit, so an episodic request arriving during it is not scheduled until the step that produces the cold request's first token. The chain Part C tests is: (1) if the materialization is split into prefix-chained slices then the longest non-preemptive unit falls from the whole history to one slice (StudySLICE1 Part A measured exactly this: 2.06 s -> 0.39 s at 2,048 tokens); (2) if the longest unit is shorter than the gap between episodic calls, an episodic request waits at most one slice instead of a whole prefill; (3) if slices are additionally dispatched only into gaps, the wait falls again; so (4) episodic p99 stays inside the 0.45 s budget at a higher arrival rate, which is capacity. Part C asks whether the simulator reproduces (4) on a measurement it has never seen.

Hand-checkable: a slice released 'gap' has next_episodic_due_s - now_s > pred_s, and one released 'slack' has now_s >= slack_start_s.

step4_negative_control.rule: disable the mechanism under test and the result must collapse. Slicing IS the mechanism, so P1 (the same admission queue with ONE monolithic unit) is the disabled arm and P3_2048 / P4 are the enabled ones.

mechanism_verification.step5_alternative_explanation: The headline 'P4 restores capacity' could also be produced by (b) P4 simply DELAYING the cold recall until the episodic traffic has drained, which any admission policy that waits long enough would do, rather than by slicing. The data separate them: P2 is exactly that policy - monolithic, held until its slack runs out - and it does NOT restore capacity in the measurement (< 10 % at C1a) while its answers slide to a 9.8 s median; P4 restores capacity AND answers at a 3.4-8.2 s median. A second alternative, (c) that the chain is simply CHEAPER, is excluded by Part A: chain / monolithic engine time is 0.990-1.093, so the chain costs the same or slightly more. If P4 and P2 had the same capacity the experiment could not distinguish them, and that is reported per configuration.

cold_rate_sensitivity.rule: the cold prefill rate is the one workload constant where two committed measurements disagree: StudyRH5 Part A's 4,500 tok/s at 11k (the simulator's own constant, PRIMARY) and StudySLICE1 Part A's 5,375 tok/s on this server. Both are held-in; neither is a Part B number.

p5_entry_point.how: add 'P5' to POLICIES, give build_parts a P5 branch (warm appends deferred and coalesced) and add a P5 case to _release_time (escalations gap-aligned). Nothing else changes: run_cell, cell_median and capacity are policy-agnostic, and part_c() iterates S.POLICIES.
